Plot a detection model or a detection field

Source: R/plot.R
plot.de_model.Rd

plot.de_model() draws detection probability against distance, one line per tag model and receiver depth asked for. plot.de_field() maps one receiver's detection probability over the water cells, or the probability that at least one receiver detects a transmission from each cell when every receiver listens. The whole array is drawn on the fixed scale 0 to 1. A single receiver is drawn from 0 to its own highest probability, so that a receiver peaking near 0.5 is readable. Both use the magma palette.

Usage

# S3 method for de_model
plot(x, distance = NULL, depth = NA, tag_model = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for de_field
plot(x, receiver = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A de_model or a de_field.

distance

For plot.de_model(), the distances in metres to draw. By default 0 m to the distance where the last of the curves falls below 0.01, at most 20 km, so every curve is drawn past its d05.

depth, tag_model

For plot.de_model(), receiver depths and tag models; one line per combination. By default tag_model is every tag model the detection model knows.

...

Not used. Change the figure by adding ggplot2 layers, scales or ggplot2::labs() to the plot it returns.

receiver

For plot.de_field(), the key of the receiver to map, or NULL to map the coverage of the whole array.

Value

A ggplot object. It prints when not assigned; assign it to add layers or to save it with ggplot2::ggsave().

Details

Both methods build the figure with ggplot2 and theme_positionr(). The map draws the probability with scale_fill_probability(), the magma palette of every positionR probability map, the receivers as open circles in the viridis yellow "#FDE725" over a thin dark edge, the glyph of a detecting receiver in plot.loc_surface(), so they read on the dark and the pale ends of magma (the mapped receiver larger), equal coordinates and a scale bar at the bottom right. Land is left blank. The map spans the field's water cells and its receivers, so a grid cut wider than the water draws no empty margin. Axis titles name the grid's coordinate reference system, as in plot.loc_surface().

Examples

# The curve of the Stoney example at the shallowest, a middle and the
# deepest receiver.
m <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
plot(m, depth = c(1, 13, 25))


# The Stoney example: Stoney Lake (100 m cells, land NA) and 70 receivers.
tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield")
grid <- terra::rast(tif)
curve <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
# Beyond 2 km the Stoney curve is below 0.001 at every receiver; leaving
# those pairs out keeps the example quick.
field <- de_field(water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers,
                                  max_distance = 2000), curve)
#> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
plot(field, receiver = "S005")

plot(field)
